subject: Unexpected 429s — tenant routing map mismatch and next steps
body:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchid-analytics.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 429s from our production tenant (tenant: orchid-prod)

Hi Vivek —

We started seeing a significant number of 429 responses from Redwood for our production tenant (orchid-prod) starting ~07:58 PDT. This is impacting inference-heavy endpoints (chat and embeddings) across multiple services. We haven't changed traffic patterns on our side. Could you confirm whether this is on Redwood's end and what the mitigation plan is?

We can provide logs if helpful.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Platform
Orchid Analytics

---
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchid-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:22:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike of 429s from our production tenant (tenant: orchid-prod)

Hi Priya —

Thanks for flagging this and sorry for the interruption. We are currently triaging. Initial check shows a sudden increase in 429s correlated to our quota-routing translation layer for the tenant map — a configuration change deployed this morning inadvertently included orchid-prod in a generic routing rule that applied stricter token windows.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Rolling a hotfix to revert the problematic routing translation (ETA ~20 minutes).
- Enabling an override rule to accept in-flight sessions for orchid-prod while the fix deploys.
- Our SREs will monitor for residual 429s and follow up with a short postmortem.

Can you share any specific request IDs or timestamps if you have them (a few sample request_ids would help correlate logs)?

I'll follow up with a status update in ~30 minutes and share the mitigation checklist.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike of 429s from our production tenant (tenant: orchid-prod)

Priya, Vivek —

We pushed the revert and the override at 08:35 PDT. You should see a rapid drop in 429s after that change. A few notes on why this manifested: a recent optimization to compress tenant mapping into a compact rule set omitted an exception that preserves existing tenant quotas. That omission caused orchid-prod to be matched by the stricter bucket.

What I did:
- Reverted the mapping commit that introduced the exclusion regression.
- Temporarily raised the token window for orchid-prod to match the pre-change profile.
- Instruments were added to trace the mapping decision for every request for the next 2 hours.

If you still see 429s after now, please send two or three request_ids and timestamps and I'll pull the traces immediately.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchid-analytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:12:03 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: root cause, corrective steps, and compensatory credits for orchid-prod 429 spike

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the quick signal — appreciated. Below is a concise summary and next steps. Full postmortem is attached.

What happened (TL;DR):
- Root cause: A recent deployment to our tenant-routing translation layer introduced a rule consolidation optimization that inadvertently removed a tenant-specific exclusion for orchid-prod. As a result, requests from orchid-prod matched a more restrictive quota bucket and received 429s.
- Impact window: 2027-06-15 07:58:00 PDT to 2027-06-15 08:36:00 PDT.
- Scope: Approximately 6.2% of requests from orchid-prod returned 429s during the window; no data exposure or model degradation occurred.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Reverted the offending mapping at 08:35 PDT and applied a temporary override.
- Instrumented request-level mapping logs and added an alert that triggers if >1% of a tenant's requests return 429 within a 5-minute sliding window.
- Added an automated canary check during mapping deploys that validates exclusions for known production tenants.

Planned long-term fixes (next 30 days):
- Add a regression test suite for tenant-exclusion rules and validate against a snapshot of production tenant manifests.
- Implement formal change gating for mapping changes (code owner approvals + automated integration test).
- Update runbook: include customer-facing escalation steps and a templated credit policy for transient quota misclassification incidents.

Compensation and next steps:
- We're preparing a one-time service credit for the impacted window; attached is a preliminary credit statement (CSV). We'll finalize the credit amount once you confirm the usage window you'd like credited (options: full-window or per-429 credit).
- Please review the attached postmortem (ORCHID-20270615) and mitigation checklist. We plan a short follow-up call on Thu Jun 17 at 09:00 PDT if that works for your team.

Attachments: 20270617-postmortem-orchid-incident.md, 20270617-credit-statement-ORCHID.csv

I will remain the SRE point of contact for this item; looping in Lauren for commercial follow-up on credits.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
